content.text:
I submitted **index 34 (Fe 0.39, Ni 0.18, V 0.42)** as the best composition. It had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, at 2.8 µA. With only three merit measurements among 160 compositions, I don't know how close it is to the best in the library.

| Index | Composition (Fe / Ni / V) | Photocurrent | XRD reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| **34** | 0.39 / 0.18 / 0.42 | **2.8e-6 A** | Probably an FeVO4-like phase (extra peaks at Q ≈ 1.93, 2.30, 2.50) |
| 5 | 0.22 / 0.18 / 0.60 | 1.82e-6 A | Many extra peaks, so probably several V-rich phases |
| 56 | 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.20 | 7.9e-7 A | Fe-rich; peaks look like hematite or a spinel |
| 1 | 0.15 / 0.72 / 0.13 | not measured | Mostly Ni oxide |

**How I chose:**
- **XRD first.** I used 4 of the 5 XRD measurements on corners of the composition space. Every pattern shares the same set of peaks (Q ≈ 1.878, 2.374, 2.649, 3.559 …), which I took to be the SnO2/FTO substrate. The phase assignments in the table come from the peaks left over after removing those, matched from memory rather than a database, so they are tentative.
- **Photocurrent.** I measured the three low-Ni compositions: Fe-V near 1:1 (34), V-rich (5) and Fe-rich (56). I skipped the Ni-rich corner because Ni-rich oxides are generally poor photoanodes.

**Main gap:** I didn't test anything close to index 34. Nearby low-Ni compositions such as 94, 82 and 118 might do better, but they are unmeasured and would earn nothing under the scoring. The one remaining XRD measurement went unused.
